overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals clear audience preference for space, cosmic anomaly, and 'what-if planetary fall' scenarios. Videos featuring extreme space phenomena (such as liquid diamond planets, dark planets, extreme weather on exoplanets, and unusual planetary timelines) consistently achieve higher velocity in views-per-day and stronger engagement rates (likes-per-view) compared to older or standard psychology/animal trivia. Specifically, hypothetical physics/cosmology questions and bizarre planetary environments dominate the top tier of recent traction.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) generate high engagement and steady view velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space survival and exotic exoplanet scenarios with high-stakes visual hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing impossible environments such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,027 views) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (980 views) outperform standard space facts.
winning_patterns.action: Continue sourcing bizarre, verifiable astrophysical extremes focusing on physics defying normal human intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content focusing on standard psychological tricks or memory hacks (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') stagnation at very low views (<55 views) and zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological trivia unless paired with a high-concept, cinematic narrative hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts ('Octopuses Have THREE Hearts') have plateaued in growth momentum compared to novel space concepts.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than basic trivia.
